headline.purpose: The name of the open entry.

lead.purpose: The statement on the first view; the Ask answer is set at the same scale.

body.purpose: Entry paragraphs and the intro above a list; 1rem / 1.5 on short screens.

ui.purpose: Bar links, list rows, fact rows, text links, citation rows.

meta.purpose: The line under an entry name, authors and venue, the pager, quiet actions, the Ask button label (at 600).

label.purpose: The heading of a group within a list; at 400, the aside at the right of a row.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The --ease token: every arrival animation (parts of words, fades, bar, Ask strip).

motion.name: arrive
motion.value: 0.55s var(--ease) both; from opacity 0, blur(5px), translateY(0.14em)
motion.purpose: One part of a word arriving. Parts are two or three letters; the default interval is 22ms, shortened so a run ends within its cap (default 1100ms).

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Lists, meta lines, links and the portrait fade in, lightly staggered. The bar and Ask strip use it once at 0.9s (strip delayed 0.3s).

motion.name: later-pace
motion.purpose: After the first move between views the sequence plays fast. The Ask answer keeps the full pace; fades in the answer view wait 500ms.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, background-colour and underline-colour changes on hover. Nothing moves on interaction.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All arrival animations are off; the finished page shows at once.

narrative.overview:
The whole site is one screen that does not scroll: a bar, the view, and a field to ask a question. There is one ground, one ink, a soft grey for whatever is secondary, and hairlines where two regions meet. Everything a visitor reads is set in a serif built for scientific publishing; everything they operate is set in a plain sans. The page is a sheet of text with nothing on it that is not text, a rule, or the one portrait.

Restraint is a rule of this system, not a mood. It was asked for directly, after an ornate build was rejected: much simpler, less content, less motion, quieter colour and type, no scrolling. A new surface earns its place by removing something, and anything added has to be made of the materials already here (a word, an underline, a hairline, a change from soft to ink). The single flourish the system allows itself is how text arrives: a part of a word at a time, quickly, then still.

Rejected by the user and not to return: the decorated portfolio (plates, panels, ornament, a display face for show, a bright signal colour) and the long scrolling portfolio.
keyCharacteristics: One screen, three rows: bar, view, Ask strip. Views change in place; the address hash carries the view and the open entry.
One ground, one ink, one soft grey, two hairline weights of grey, one blue that only marks attention.
Two faces: STIX Two Text for what is read, Archivo for what is operated.
No panels, no shadows, no radius, no icons. Links are underlined words; controls are words.
Text arrives a part of a word at a time; lists and small print only fade.
Light only (`color-scheme: light`); there is no dark theme.

rules.name: The Restraint Rule
rules.body: Nothing is added that the reading does not need. Before adding a colour, a weight, a size, a container or a movement, try the existing soft-to-ink change, an underline, or a hairline. If those cannot carry it, the thing probably does not belong on this page.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue marks where attention is right now: focus, the caret, the citation under the pointer. If a blue thing would still be blue with nobody touching the page, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Soft-to-Ink Rule
rules.body: Choices rest in Soft Grey and become Ink when hovered or current. The current one also takes a 1px underline. That change is the entire selection vocabulary; there is no highlight bar, fill, or marker.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: The only emphatic state is swapping Ink and Paper: the text selection, the skip link, and the Ask button under the pointer. No third colour is used for emphasis.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: If it is read, it is STIX Two Text. If it is operated or is small print about something read, it is Archivo. A third family is never introduced, and neither face is used for the other's job.

rules.name: The Plain Setting Rule
rules.body: Sentence case everywhere. No uppercase, no positive letter-spacing, no small caps. Weight is 400 by default; 600 appears only on the name in the bar, publication titles, group headings and the Ask button. Italic is for a venue or a title within text, never for emphasis by habit.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: The page never scrolls. New content gets a view in the bar, an entry in a list, or a page within an entry; it never gets length.

rules.name: The One Thing Rule
rules.body: When there is not room for the list and the entry together, show one, with a worded way back. Do not shrink both to fit.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits on top of anything. If a design needs a surface above the page (a modal, a popover, a card, a drawer), it becomes a view instead.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A line is 1px and horizontal, in Hairline between regions and Strong Hairline under words. Lines never enclose content; the Ask button is the only outlined box on the page.

rules.name: The Arrival Rule
rules.body: Motion is how text arrives and nothing else. Only read text gets the part-by-part reveal; everything else fades; nothing moves in response to hover, scroll or selection.

dos: Do keep the page to one viewport: bar, view, Ask strip. Add a view, an entry or a page within an entry instead of length.
Do set everything read in STIX Two Text and everything operated in Archivo, in sentence case, at weight 400 unless it is one of the four places that take 600.
Do show choice by the Soft-to-Ink change plus a 1px underline on the current item.
Do separate regions with a 1px Hairline and items with space (6, 14, 16, 22px).
Do write controls as words: "Back to the list", "Continue", "Close", "3 more sources".
Do keep Attention Blue to focus, the caret, the focused Ask strip and citation hover.
Do say failures and gaps in a plain sentence in the place they occur (the graph is offline; GitHub didn't answer this hour).
Do give every animation a reduced-motion state that shows the finished page at once.
donts: Don't add panels, cards, tinted areas, shadows, gradients, rounded corners, or anything that sits above the page. The only fill is the inversion to Ink.
Don't add icons, arrows, glyph bullets or emoji as interface; an action is its word.
Don't add a second accent, a tinted background, or blue on anything at rest.
Don't introduce a third typeface, uppercase labels, tracked-out small print, or a display face for show.
Don't let the document scroll, and don't use a view-level scrollbar as a design choice; it exists only as a last resort.
Don't animate on hover, scroll or selection, and don't make navigation wait for the reveal.
Don't bring back ornament from the retired builds: plates, charts, borders that enclose content, a bright signal colour.
Don't add images beyond the one portrait without a decision to change this system.
